items.title: Iran faces leadership vacuum after Khamenei killed in U.S.-Israeli strikes

featured_image.name: A placard calling for regime change in Iran

items.description:
The killing of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in joint U.S.-Israeli strikes on Saturday has plunged the Islamic Republic into its deepest leadership crisis since the 1979 revolution, with no clear successor and competing factions already maneuvering for power.

Iranian state television and the state-run IRNA news agency confirmed the 86-year-old's death early Sunday, following what President Donald Trump described as "major combat operations" launched alongside Israel against Iranian military and government targets. Trump called the moment "the single greatest chance for the Iranian people to take back their Country".[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Iran forms temporary leadership council after Khamenei killed in US-Israeli strikes

featured_image.name: Trump Says Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei Is Dead

items.description:
Iran has set in motion its constitutional succession process after state television confirmed that Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed during coordinated US-Israeli airstrikes on Saturday, marking the most profound rupture in the Islamic Republic since its founding nearly five decades ago.

A temporary leadership council composed of President Masoud Pezeshkian, judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei, and a jurist member of the Guardian Council — selected by the Expediency Discernment Council — has assumed the duties of the supreme leader, according to Iranian state news agency IRNA. Mohammad Mokhber, one of Khamenei's advisers, confirmed in a televised interview that the transition was being carried out under Article 111 of Iran's constitution, which governs the interim period following a supreme leader's death.[1][2][3]

items.title: Regional toll mounts as Iran and Israel trade strikes through the day

featured_image.name: Iran fires missiles at Israel in retaliation for strikes on ...

items.description:
Iran launched waves of ballistic missiles and drones at Israel and multiple Gulf Arab nations on Saturday, hours after the United States and Israel began a joint military offensive against Iranian targets that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and struck military and nuclear sites across the country.

The Iranian counterattack targeted not only Israel but also US military bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, and Jordan, marking one of the broadest regional escalations in decades. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps vowed the strikes would continue "until the enemy is conclusively vanquished".[1]

items.title: Airport deaths reported as Iran retaliates for US-Israeli strikes

featured_image.name: U.S. and Israel's attack on Iran disrupt flights across the Middle East and beyond as airspaces close

items.description:
Coordinated military strikes by the United States and Israel against Iran on Saturday, February 28, brought commercial aviation across the Middle East to a near-standstill, stranding tens of thousands of travelers worldwide and forcing airlines from every continent to cancel, divert, or reroute flights.

At least eight countries — Iran, Israel, Iraq, Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait, Jordan, and the United Arab Emirates — closed their airspace in the hours following the strikes, which began around 1:15 a.m. EST. Flight tracking data from Flightradar24 showed the skies over much of the region virtually empty of commercial traffic by Saturday afternoon. Preliminary data from aviation analytics firm Cirium, cited by Reuters, indicated that nearly 40 percent of flights to Dubai and a comparable share of flights to the wider region were cancelled on Saturday alone.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Pakistan rules out talks with Afghanistan as fighting enters third day

featured_image.name: Afghanistan says Pakistan fighter jet down as cross-border ...

items.description:
Pakistan and Afghanistan continued to exchange fire along their contested border on Saturday, with Islamabad ruling out negotiations and demanding Kabul end its alleged support for militant groups, as the most serious military confrontation between the two neighbors in years showed no signs of abating.

Pakistan's prime minister's spokesperson told Pakistani television on Saturday that "there won't be talks" and "there's no negotiation," insisting Afghanistan must first cease harboring militants. The statement came despite the Taliban government expressing willingness to resolve the crisis through dialogue. The European Union's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas also urged both nations Saturday to lower tensions, warning the violence could destabilize the wider region.[1]

items.title: Trump backs regime change as Iran strikes continue

featured_image.name: Trump deliberated on Iran for weeks. His 'massive and ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday openly urged the Iranian people to overthrow their government, following a joint U.S.-Israeli military operation that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and devastated military targets across the country.

In a video posted to Truth Social, Trump told Iranians, "When we are finished, take over your government. It will be yours to take. This will be probably your only chance for generations". He later called Khamenei's death "the single greatest opportunity for the Iranian people to reclaim their Country" and said that reports indicated many members of Iran's security forces were already seeking terms.[1][2][3]

Netanyahu, in a nationally televised address, called on Iranians to "flood the streets and finish the job," describing the moment as a "once-in-a-generation opportunity" to dismantle the regime.[4][5]

items.title: Trump says Khamenei is dead after US-Israel strikes on Iran

featured_image.name: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Iran's Supreme Leader, Killed in US ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump declared Saturday that Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei had been killed in coordinated US-Israeli strikes on Iran, posting on Truth Social that "Khamenei, one of the most evil people in History, is dead". Iran has denied the claim, with its foreign minister calling the reports "mental warfare."[1]

The announcement followed hours of uncertainty after the United States and Israel launched a sweeping military operation against Iran in the early hours of February 28, targeting military installations, air defenses, and government compounds across Tehran, Isfahan, Qom, and other cities. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a televised address that there were "growing signs" Khamenei had been killed when Israeli forces struck his compound in Tehran. Two senior Israeli officials subsequently told the Associated Press that Israel had confirmed his death and that his body had been recovered.[2][3]

items.title: Israel says Khamenei killed in joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran

featured_image.name: US and Isreal launch a major attack on Iran

items.description:
Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed Saturday in a massive joint U.S.-Israeli military operation targeting Tehran and cities across Iran, according to multiple Israeli officials. A senior Israeli official told Reuters that Khamenei's body had been found in the ruins of his compound. Israeli Ambassador to Washington Yechiel Leiter confirmed the killing to U.S. officials, according to Axios reporter Barak Ravid.[1][2][3]

The 86-year-old Khamenei, who had led the Islamic Republic since 1989, was struck in the opening salvo of the operation as Israeli and American forces simultaneously hit three separate gatherings of senior Iranian officials, an Israeli military official told reporters. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Donald Trump were both shown an image of Khamenei's body recovered from his compound, Israel's Channel 12 reported.[4][5][1]

items.title: FBI on high alert as U.S., Israel strike Iran

featured_image.name: Iran Strikes: Kash Patel Puts FBI Counterterrorism Teams on ...

items.description:
FBI Director Kash Patel placed the bureau's counterterrorism and counterintelligence teams on high alert Saturday after the United States and Israel launched coordinated military strikes on Iran in what the Pentagon has dubbed "Operation Epic Fury."

"FBI personnel are fully engaged on the situation overseas. Last night I instructed our Counterterrorism and intelligence teams to be on high alert and mobilize all assisting security assets needed," Patel wrote on X. "Our JTTFs throughout the country are working 24/7, as always, to address and disrupt any potential threats to the homeland."[1]

The directive came as U.S. Central Command confirmed that strikes began at 1:15 a.m. ET on February 28, targeting Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps command facilities, air defense systems, missile launch sites, and military airfields across Iran.[2]
